draft.title: Major muscles
card: Quadriceps
the muscles on the front of the thigh. They extend the knee, as when you kick a ball.
Hamstrings
the muscles on the back of the thigh. They flex the knee, bringing the heel towards the buttocks.
Deltoids
the muscles that cover the shoulder. They lift the arm out to the side and also forwards and backwards.
Biceps
the muscle on the front of the upper arm. It flexes the elbow, as when you curl a weight towards your shoulder.
draft.remember: Match each muscle to its place and its movement: quadriceps extend the knee, hamstrings flex it, deltoids lift the arm, biceps flex the elbow.

a.q: Which muscle group mainly flexes the knee, pulling the heel towards the buttocks?
a.why: The hamstrings are on the back of the thigh and flex the knee. The quadriceps are on the front of the thigh and do the opposite, extending the knee.
a.clue: Look at the back of the thigh.

b.q: Tom is a netball player. He straightens his knee to push off the ground for a jump. Which muscle group is mainly working at his knee?
b.why: Straightening the knee is extension, and the quadriceps on the front of the thigh do this. The hamstrings are tempting because they are also in the thigh, but they flex the knee instead.

problems.detail: To answer, the student must link 'straightens his knee' to extension. That link is a movement term from point 5, and the card never says that extending the knee means straightening it. The clue then defines the term ('Straightening a joint is extension'), which explains a term that belongs to another point in the chapter.

check.summary: The facts on the card and both answers are correct. The only issue is question b: it relies on the clue to define extension as straightening, a movement term from point 5 that the card does not teach.

proposal.title: Major muscles
card: Quadriceps
the muscles on the front of the thigh. They straighten the leg at the knee, as when you kick a ball.
Hamstrings
the muscles on the back of the thigh. They bend the knee, bringing the heel towards the buttocks.
Deltoids
the muscles that cover the shoulder. They raise the arm out to the side and help move it forwards and backwards.
Biceps
the muscle on the front of the upper arm. It bends the elbow, as when you curl a weight towards your shoulder.
proposal.remember: Front of the thigh straightens the knee, back bends it. Deltoids move the arm at the shoulder, biceps bend the elbow.

a.q: A sprinter's heel swings up behind her towards her buttocks as her knee bends. Which muscle group mainly does this?
a.why: The hamstrings are on the back of the thigh and bend the knee, lifting the heel towards the buttocks. The quadriceps are also in the thigh, but they are on the front and straighten the knee instead.
a.clue: Which side of the thigh pulls the heel up behind?

b.q: Tom is a netball player. He straightens his knee to push off the ground for a jump. Which muscle group is mainly working at his knee?
b.why: The quadriceps on the front of the thigh straighten the leg at the knee, which drives Tom upwards. The hamstrings are tempting because they are also in the thigh, but they bend the knee rather than straighten it.
b.clue: Which thigh muscles straighten the leg, as in a kick?

problems.detail: To answer, the student must link 'straightens his knee' to extension. That link is a movement term from point 5, and the card never says that extending the knee means straightening it. The clue then defines the term ('Straightening a joint is extension'), which explains a term that belongs to another point in the chapter.
